title: observability(api): propagate request-id & trace context, structured logs, endpoint metrics tags, OpenAI-compat streaming stability
author: Avery Chen
description: Summary: Add end-to-end observability improvements on the public API surface. This PR propagates a stable request-id header through gateways and the runtime, forwards trace context (W3C traceparent/tracestate) into internal spans, converts API gateway logs to structured JSON with request-level fields, and attaches per-endpoint tags to metrics so dashboards and alerts can slice by public routes. It also includes compatibility fixes for our OpenAI-compat streaming layer to ensure request-id and trace headers are preserved across streaming proxying and function/tool-calling code paths. Motivation: Customers and SREs need reliable request-scoped telemetry to debug streaming issues and trace multi-hop requests (API gateway -> compat proxy -> runtime -> backend). Previously request-ids were generated in multiple places and lost during streaming/function calls; tracing context was inconsistently propagated, and metrics could not be grouped by external API routes. Changes in this PR: - Add X-Request-ID canonical header generation at the ingress with deterministic fallback to trace id when missing. - Ensure W3C traceparent/tracestate headers are accepted at the gateway and injected into the runtime tracing context. - Thread request-id into structured logs emitted by gateway, proxy, runtime, and worker processes as top-level JSON fields (request_id, path, method, user_id when present, model). - Add per-endpoint metric label/tagging on all API metrics (latency, tokens_consumed, errors) using the external route name (openai.chat.completions, generation.stream, embeddings.create). - Fix OpenAI-compat streaming proxy to preserve headers and to propagate request-id on chunked events, ensure function-calling tool invocation includes traceparent. - Add unit and integration tests for header propagation, structured log formatting, and metrics labels. - Add migrations to dashboards: update existing API latency dashboard to include endpoint tag. - Docs: update API observability docs with examples for trace propagation and structured logs. Checklist: - [x] Generate/propagate canonical request-id at ingress - [x] Preserve headers through OpenAI-compat streaming proxy - [x] Thread trace context into runtime spans - [x] Structured JSON logs for API surface - [x] Per-endpoint metrics tagging - [x] Tests for propagation and labels - [x] Update dashboards and docs Notes and rationale: request-id uses X-Request-ID if present; if absent we derive from trace-id for backward compatibility. We intentionally do not expose internal trace IDs to external clients but will map them when allowed by customer config. Compatibility: This is backwards-compatible for callers; clients that rely on prior opaque request-id behavior shouldn't break. Streaming behavior: added integration test covering the common streaming code path and a flaky test harness which was stabilized by adding a short header-copy flush in the proxy (race condition fix). Observability impact: Adds ~0.8% CPU overhead at gateway due to JSON logging in high throughput paths; this was measured in perf-canary and is acceptable given debugging gains. Rollout plan: feature flag 'observability.external-tracing' initially enabled for 10% of traffic, then 50%, then full roll. Monitoring alerts will watch any increase in gateway latency or 5xx rate post-rollout. Related: ENG-4821 (API observability epic), ENG-4830 (OpenAI-compat streaming stability).
commits: feat(obs): add canonical request-id generation at ingress
fix(compat): preserve headers during streaming proxying
feat(logging): structured JSON output for api gateway logs
feat(metrics): attach endpoint tag to api metrics
test: add integration tests for header and trace propagation
review_comments: Samir Patel: Can you clarify why we map to trace-id when X-Request-ID is missing? Is there risk of exposing trace ids?

Avery Chen (author): We only derive a local request-id from trace-id to have a stable value across services. We don't return internal trace ids to the client unless the feature flag is enabled for a customer; mapping is internal for logs/metrics only.
Maya Rodriguez: The structured logger change looks good, but ensure we avoid expensive serialization on hot paths. Can we reuse buffer pools?
Avery Chen (author): Implemented buffer pooling in json_logger.go and added microbenchmarks. See logging buffer pool commit.
Lars Jensen: I ran perf-canary on a 2h window; CPU bump at gateway is visible but within our SLO. Approve after tests are green.
Samir Patel: Please add an integration test that streams a function-calling invocation and asserts request-id is present in the tool invocation trace.
Avery Chen (author): Added integration test in integration-tests/observability/header-propagation.test.ts that covers function-calls and streaming chunks.
release_notes: Adds request-id propagation (X-Request-ID), W3C traceparent propagation, structured JSON logs for the API surface, and per-endpoint metric tags. Improves OpenAI-compat streaming stability by preserving headers across streaming proxying. Backwards compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
